answer: Sybil resistance via vouching quorums: a new agent cannot transact until K established peers vouch, each locking collateral on it. If proven synthetic, part of every voucher's stake is burnt. Attackers must persuade real staked identities, so each fake identity adds bonded cost linearly. Like a comet, a cheap bot swarm burns bright, then evaporates when slashing lands. Attacker expense peaks at its zenith in verification windows, as duplicated behavior exposes clusters. Honest agents keep their reputation kernel intact, while one more fake identity soon costs more than any reward.
